editorial: Singapore is expensive by Southeast Asian standards and can become expensive very quickly if you treat every meal, attraction and hotel as a splurge.
Our most spectacular food overspend was about SGD200 for two at Gyu-Kaku. Housing prices we heard from friends were on another planet entirely, but thankfully tourists only rent rooms by the night.
Hawker meals and excellent public transport are the budget counterweight. The country can be done sensibly if luxury malls remain sightseeing rather than shopping.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: Stay centrally, eat one or two serious meals and buy convenience: taxis when tired, premium zoo experiences and a hotel with a good view.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: Lean hard into hawker centres and the MRT, and be selective with ticketed attractions. Singapore's best urban experience—walking around a functioning city—is largely free.

title: What it's Going to Cost
